name: Stochastic Top-k Relaxation and Gumbel-Top-k
key_paper: Kool, W., van Hoof, H., & Welling, M. (2019). Stochastic Beams and Where to Find Them: The Gumbel-Top-k Trick for Sampling Sequences Without Replacement. NeurIPS 2019. Secondary: Xie, S. M., & Ermon, S. (2019). Reparameterizable Subset Sampling via Continuous Relaxations. IJCAI 2019. Also relevant: Pervez, A., & Tonolini, F. (2023). Differentiable Top-k Classification Learning. ICML 2023.
algorithm_description: Gumbel-top-k is a method for exactly sampling k items without replacement from a categorical distribution in a single forward pass. The trick: add i.i.d. Gumbel(0,1) noise to the log-probabilities of all N items, then take the top-k indices by perturbed score. This produces an exact sample from the distribution of k items drawn without replacement proportional to their probabilities (Plackett-Luce model). The stochastic top-k relaxation makes this differentiable: instead of a hard argmax over the perturbed scores, a soft (temperature-annealed) approximation is used so that gradients can flow back through the selection process. Pervez and Tonolini (2023) extend this to a fully differentiable top-k operator with a smooth surrogate that converges to the exact top-k as temperature goes to zero, enabling end-to-end training of models whose output is a ranked or unranked subset of k items.
action_space_handling: The method treats the action space as a flat categorical distribution over N items (e.g., N=50 ball pool), assigns a learned score/logit to each item, and selects k items jointly in one shot by perturbing all logits with Gumbel noise and taking the top-k. This is a joint, non-autoregressive selection — all k items are chosen simultaneously without sequential conditioning. The probability of any particular subset of size k is given by the Plackett-Luce model, which is tractable and well-studied. The approach avoids the exponential action space of joint enumeration while still respecting the combinatorial structure.
how_combinatorial_output_is_formed: A neural network (e.g., the SharedLotteryTransformer) produces N logits, one per ball. During training, i.i.d. Gumbel(0,1) noise is added to each logit, and a differentiable soft-top-k operator (e.g., using the regularized optimal transport formulation or temperature-softmax approximation) selects k items in a differentiable manner. During inference, the hard top-k of perturbed logits gives an exact Plackett-Luce sample without replacement. Multiple plays are generated by running multiple independent Gumbel perturbation draws, giving diverse outputs that correctly reflect the learned probability distribution over subsets.
sequential_generation_strategy: Joint (flat, non-autoregressive). All k numbers in a play are selected simultaneously in one forward pass rather than one at a time. This means inter-number correlations within a draw are not explicitly modeled — the joint probability factorizes via the Plackett-Luce model over independent logits. This is simpler and faster than autoregressive generation but sacrifices the ability to model co-occurrence patterns between specific ball pairs. For the lottery application, this is generally acceptable since co-occurrence structure in ~100 draws is too weak to model reliably anyway.
gradient_estimator_type: Reparameterization / Gumbel reparameterization. The Gumbel perturbation acts as a reparameterization trick for the Plackett-Luce distribution, analogous to Gumbel-softmax for categorical variables. Gradients flow through the soft relaxation of the top-k operator back to the logit-producing network with low variance. This is strictly lower variance than REINFORCE/score-function estimators for the same task because the reparameterization gradient has no need for a baseline correction. The bias-variance tradeoff is controlled by the temperature parameter: lower temperature gives less bias (closer to hard top-k) but slightly higher variance.
combinatorial_constraint_enforcement: Distinctness (no repeats) is guaranteed by construction: the Gumbel-top-k selects the k highest-ranked items from N distinct candidates, so duplicate selection is impossible. The constraint that exactly k numbers are chosen is enforced by always taking exactly the top-k elements. No rejection sampling or post-hoc filtering is needed. This is one of the key advantages over softmax-based sampling approaches (which require rejection loops to avoid duplicates) and over autoregressive masking (which requires sequential decoding).
sample_efficiency_rating: medium — The technique itself is a gradient estimator, not a sample-complexity-reducing algorithm. Its advantage is lower-variance gradients compared to REINFORCE, which translates to faster convergence per gradient step. On datasets of fewer than 200 draws, the upstream model (the transformer logit head) still needs sufficient data to learn meaningful ball probabilities. With ~100 draws per lottery, the logit network is unlikely to learn strong combinatorial patterns regardless of how clean the gradient signal is. However, Gumbel-top-k avoids the high-variance gradient noise of REINFORCE, which would be especially harmful on small datasets, so it is preferable to score-function estimators in this regime.
regularization_built_in: Temperature annealing provides implicit regularization: at high temperature the soft-top-k is nearly uniform over all subsets (high entropy), constraining the model from over-committing to narrow modes early in training. The Gumbel noise itself acts as a stochastic perturbation that prevents deterministic collapse during training. No explicit entropy bonus, KL penalty, or dropout is built into the core technique — these must be added externally. Entropy of the Plackett-Luce distribution can be computed in closed form and added as an auxiliary loss to encourage exploration.
known_failure_modes_on_small_data: Mode collapse: with few training examples, the logit network may quickly over-fit to the empirical frequency of a small number of balls, causing the learned distribution to collapse onto a narrow subset regardless of Gumbel noise. Gradient saturation: if logits become very large in magnitude, the soft relaxation approaches the hard top-k and gradients through the soft operator vanish (similar to straight-through estimator collapse). Reward sparsity amplification: Gumbel-top-k improves gradient quality but does not solve the problem that the reward signal (lottery hits) is nearly always zero; with fewer than 200 training draws this sparsity is extreme. Temperature schedule sensitivity: choosing too fast an annealing schedule on small data causes the relaxation to harden before the model has converged.

data_regime_evidence.minimum_training_samples_tested: Kool et al. 2019 validated on sequence-to-sequence tasks and combinatorial optimization benchmarks (TSP, VRP) with thousands of training instances. Pervez and Tonolini 2023 tested on image classification and ranking datasets with standard large-scale benchmarks. Neither paper tests the pure Gumbel-top-k subset sampling primitive specifically on fewer than 200 training samples as a standalone RL/policy-learning setup.
data_regime_evidence.performance_degradation_curve: [uncertain] — No published degradation curve for the lottery-relevant regime (n < 200, sparse reward, combinatorial output). Expected: gradient variance advantage over REINFORCE shrinks as the dataset grows, so the relative benefit of Gumbel-top-k is highest on small data; however absolute learning signal is also weakest there.
data_regime_evidence.comparison_baseline: Compared to REINFORCE with baseline in Kool et al. 2019: Gumbel-top-k beam search produces better diversity and likelihood estimates on sequence generation tasks. Compared to Gumbel-softmax (with replacement): Gumbel-top-k respects the without-replacement constraint exactly, which is critical for lottery (no repeated balls).

convergence_guarantees_small_n: No finite-sample convergence bounds are provided in the Kool et al. 2019 or Pervez and Tonolini 2023 papers for the small-data regime. The technique provides an unbiased gradient estimator for the relaxed (soft) objective and a consistent estimator as temperature approaches zero, but these are asymptotic properties. In practice with n < 200 training draws, convergence is empirically sensitive to learning rate, temperature schedule, and model capacity. No theoretical guarantees distinguish it from other reparameterization-based estimators in the finite-sample setting. [uncertain]
reward_distribution_handling: Gumbel-top-k is a policy gradient technique and inherits standard policy gradient challenges with sparse rewards. It does not natively handle skewed reward distributions — a separate reward shaping or baseline mechanism must be added (e.g., a Critic network, a running mean baseline, or z-score normalization of returns). The method does not support distributional returns natively. Minimum draws for stable policy learning in a sparse-reward lottery setting is likely 500+ when used alone; pairing with semi-bandit number-level feedback (which ball in the predicted set actually hit) substantially reduces the effective sample requirement.
credit_assignment_granularity: By default, Gumbel-top-k operates at play level — a single reward is assigned to the entire selected subset. However, because the Plackett-Luce model assigns a factored probability to each item, it is possible to decompose the gradient by item: the gradient with respect to ball i's logit is proportional to its indicator (was it selected?) weighted by the reward. This enables semi-bandit credit assignment — each ball that appeared in a winning subset receives a positive gradient signal proportional to its contribution, enabling number-level credit without requiring a separate architecture.
diversity_mechanism: Diversity arises naturally from the stochastic Gumbel perturbation: each forward pass draws fresh i.i.d. Gumbel noise, producing a different subset even if the underlying logits are identical. The temperature parameter controls diversity: at high temperature, selections are nearly uniformly random; at low temperature, plays converge toward the deterministic top-k. Multiple plays in a batch are always distinct (different Gumbel draws). An explicit entropy bonus on the Plackett-Luce distribution can be added to the loss to prevent mode collapse and ensure diversity across a session's set of generated plays.
offline_vs_online_rl_compatibility: Fully compatible with offline training. Gumbel-top-k is a differentiable sampling primitive — it requires only a dataset of (draw, reward) pairs, not live environment interaction. Training proceeds by: (1) loading historical draws, (2) computing the policy network's logits, (3) sampling plays via Gumbel-top-k, (4) computing the loss as the negative expected reward under the Plackett-Luce distribution. This is a supervised-style loop over the historical dataset with no requirement for real-time draws. This is the most critical compatibility requirement for the lottery application (one draw per week), and Gumbel-top-k satisfies it completely.
key_dependencies: PyTorch only (no additional libraries required for the core technique). The soft top-k operator can be implemented in ~30 lines of pure PyTorch using either: (a) the regularized optimal transport formulation (requires scipy for initial reference but can be PyTorch-native), or (b) a temperature-softmax approximation of the top-k indicator. Optional: torchsort (a fast differentiable sort library) can accelerate the soft-rank computation on GPU.
estimated_lines_of_code: 80-120 lines — approximately 30-40 lines for the Gumbel-top-k sampling function and soft relaxation, 20-30 lines for integration into the existing predict.py to replace the current temperature-softmax-with-rejection loop, and 20-40 lines for the policy gradient training loop (loss computation, gradient step, reward normalization).
transfer_learning_compatibility: Excellent. The existing SharedLotteryTransformer already produces per-ball logits (main_logits of shape [batch, N]). Gumbel-top-k is applied directly on top of these logits as a post-processing step — no architectural changes to the transformer backbone are required. The encoder weights are preserved and only the final logit layer (already trained) is fine-tuned via the policy gradient signal. This is a drop-in augmentation of the existing inference path, making it the most transfer-compatible technique of any examined in this research series.
specific_application_in_project: Gumbel-top-k would replace the current predict.py play generation mechanism (temperature-softmax followed by a rejection-sampling loop to avoid duplicates) with a single differentiable forward pass. Concretely: the SharedLotteryTransformer produces 50 logits per lottery head; Gumbel-top-k draws a Gumbel-perturbed sample of 7 main balls (for LottoMax) or 6 balls (for 6/49/Daily Grand) in one shot, guaranteeing no repeats and exact Plackett-Luce probabilities. This enables end-to-end differentiable training of the Actor (policy) using any reward signal derived from historical draws, replacing the current non-differentiable sampling. It is the core primitive enabling Phase 2 Actor-Critic play generation across all three lottery agents. The soft relaxation also allows the Critic to provide a differentiable loss signal directly through the selection step, enabling true Actor-Critic coupling rather than REINFORCE-style policy gradient.
replaces_or_extends: Replaces the current temperature-softmax + rejection-sampling loop in src/predict.py and main_swarm.py predict path. Extends the policy training capability by enabling gradient-based Actor updates that were not possible with the non-differentiable sampling approach.
existing_open_source_implementations: 1. Official Kool et al. implementation: github.com/wouterkool/stochastic-beams — includes Gumbel-top-k beam search for sequences. 2. torch_gumbel_top_k: small standalone PyTorch implementation available as a gist and referenced in multiple NLP repositories. 3. torchsort (github.com/teddykoker/torchsort): provides a fast GPU-compatible differentiable sort that can implement the soft top-k as argsorting soft ranks. 4. Sinkhorn top-k (github.com/ermongroup/neuralsort): the NeuralSort paper (Grover et al. 2019) provides a differentiable sorting network that subsumes top-k selection. 5. The Pervez & Tonolini 2023 ICML paper includes a reference implementation in supplementary materials. [uncertain for exact URLs — verify on GitHub before use]
benchmark_results: Kool et al. 2019 (NeurIPS): Gumbel-top-k beam search achieves better sample diversity and higher-quality solutions on TSP-20/50/100 and VRP benchmarks compared to standard beam search and REINFORCE baselines. Sequence likelihood estimation is unbiased. Pervez and Tonolini 2023 (ICML): Differentiable top-k achieves competitive accuracy on CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet top-k classification, with smoother training curves than straight-through estimators. Xie and Ermon 2019 (IJCAI): Reparameterizable subset sampling demonstrates low-variance gradient estimates on synthetic combinatorial tasks. No benchmark exists for lottery-type sparse-reward subset prediction, which is the target domain here.
notable_use_cases: 1. Combinatorial optimization: TSP, VRP, and knapsack via policy gradient with differentiable subset selection. 2. Learning-to-rank: differentiably optimizing NDCG and other rank-based metrics by treating the top-k selection as a differentiable operation. 3. Attention sparsification: selecting the top-k attention keys in a Transformer without hard masking. 4. Recommendation systems: selecting k items to recommend from a catalog of N items, maximizing a reward that is only observed for the selected set — structurally identical to lottery play generation. 5. Neural architecture search: selecting k operations from a pool of N candidates in a differentiable supernet. The recommendation system use case (k-from-N selection, sparse reward on selected items only) is the closest structural analog to lottery play generation.
